reason: The indexed primitive hexagonal metric is strong (40/40 strong lines indexed, M20 = 159), and the primary CIF parses cleanly as full-occupancy P1 Ba3In2O6 with 11 atoms (Z = 1) in the stated cell; alternative-1 likewise parses as full-occupancy P1 Ba6In4O12 (Z = 2). Primitive standardization leaves both as distinct P1 realizations in the same cell, not equivalent settings. However, neither submitted realization passes chemistry or coordinate-establishment checks. In selected.cif, periodic contacts include Ba-O = 1.417/1.428 A and O-O = 1.538 A, while the two In sites have no O neighbor closer than 3.292 and 3.568 A, respectively. Alternative-1.cif has pervasive overlaps, including Ba-O = 1.418-1.453 A, In-O = 1.419-1.428 A, O-O = 1.427 A, and In-In = 2.083 A. The trace explicitly recognized the unconstrained models as chemically unacceptable, but the submitted CIFs contain those unconstrained coordinates rather than the later chemistry-constrained refinements. Moreover, the claimed 0.9984 correlation was obtained by sampling local peak maxima only at calculated positions and retaining positions with observed intensity > 0.3; it is not a whole-profile refinement, its selected-model normalized line residual is 0.055 with individual intensity errors up to 2.94 against about 0.12 background noise, and the single charge-flip runs do not quantitatively converge onto or assign the submitted coordinates. Thus the set contains no sufficiently established chemically valid ordered realization, and another attempt is likely to add a materially different viable coordinate model.
